chunks: And Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim narrated from al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said:
“The testimony of one who possesses enmity, or one who has disgrace in religion, is not accepted.”

key_terms.ذِي شَحْنَاءَ: a person possessing hostility, rancor, or enmity
key_terms.ذِي مُخْزِيَةٍ: a person associated with disgraceful or shameful conduct
key_terms.شَهَادَةُ: testimony given by a witness in a legal or judicial setting
key_terms.فِي الدِّينِ: in matters of religion, meaning religious character and conduct
key_terms.لَا تُقْبَلُ: is not accepted or deemed valid

ai.seo_question: Whose testimony is rejected in Islamic legal rulings according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal principle regarding testimony: the witness of a person marked by enmity or by disgrace in religious conduct is not accepted. It emphasizes moral and religious integrity as necessary conditions in judicial testimony.
